To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PD research community has an opportunity to contribute to the evolution and development of ICT design into something that is more attuned to users’ interests, but that to exploit this opportunity we need to improve both our understanding of the politics-techniques gap issues and our ways of taking these issues into account in PD projects.

we need to focus on the issues that bridge politics and techniques, that there is a gap between politics and technique, that the gap is bridged, but not very well, that we need to bridge it better, that the gap will probably get wider and that we need to work on the issues in the gap.

the gap between politics (e.g., project funding) and techniques (e.g., types of users) is a crucial issue for PD and that it needs to be addressed by the PD community in order for us to contribute to the next practices of ICT design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we may develop the PD research and design practice to become more relevant to the next practices of ICT design.
how we may bridge the gap between politics, techniques and the use of PD in ICT design.
the question: How can we in the PD research community contribute to the development of ‘next practices’ in ICT design?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PD research should focus more on the politics of design and on how the politics of design can be changed.
we need to bridge the gap between politics of design and techniques of design.
we need to develop new ways to do participatory design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to bridge the gap between politics, on the one hand, and techniques, on the other hand, in the next practices of ICT design.
we need to ‘bridge the gap’ between politics and techniques.
we should focus more on issues that are ‘in the gap’ and less on the ‘traditional’ issues that are in the two sides of the gap, i.e., politics and techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to develop a much better understanding of the gap between politics, on the one hand, and techniques, on the other, and of the issues that are relevant to it.
PD is a very promising way to develop new, more democratic ways of working with ICT.
PD research is a good way to explore and to develop the new ways of doing design that are required to bridge the gap between politics of ICT and its techniques.
